summary: Cabin work had started by July 1937; a 100-ft steel tower was erected in 1938 and joined Forest Service fire detection by telephone. No source found describes the tower today.

facts.design: Steel tower of 100 feet with a lookout cabin

events.note: Work had started on the basement and cistern for the lookout's cabin by July 8, 1937 (Shannon County Democrat item, as quoted on the page).
Truck trail No. 265 being surfaced with crushed rock from Highway B to the tower (July 29, 1937 item, as quoted on the page).
Telephone line work had reached digging the holes by January 13, 1938; the line was completed by April 28, 1938, and the tower then joined the regular Forest Service fire detection network.

notes_for_editor: Every dated fact comes from one compiled page quoting 1937-38 Shannon County Democrat items; nothing found on staffing, fires, status or access. Waymarking.com's High Hill entry (WM4F8K) returned only its title, and the Chamber of Commerce listing returned 403, so neither was used. The MTNF history page did not mention the tower. Worth checking Forest Service records or recreation.gov for the tower's current status and any rental listing. The brief's 30.5 m matches the 100-foot height.
